data_output.description: data.py remains unchanged and encode(splits) returns each split as (features, labels, users), where features has five columns in canonical order user_id, video_id, tab, hour, weekday and uses the existing train-fitted offsets.

model_input.description: model.py receives the existing integer feature matrix with shape (n_rows, 5); columns 0 and 1 index separate user and video embedding tables, and columns 2 through 4 index additive tab, hour, and weekday weights. It returns one finite raw logit per input row and preserves the existing step/state/load_state interfaces.

model_designer.objective: Implement the requested 16-dimensional user-video latent-factor interaction model in model.py while retaining additive request-context scoring and the existing BCE/Adam training interface.
required_changes: Replace the separate additive contributions for encoded feature positions 0 (user_id) and 1 (video_id) with a dot product between 16-dimensional user and video embedding vectors. Use features[:, 0] as user embedding indices and features[:, 1] as video embedding indices; the latter already contains the canonical encoded offset from data.py. Allocate both embedding tables with shape (dimension, 16), allowing unused rows because data.py provides only the combined dimension.

Retain additive weights only for encoded request-context positions 2, 3, and 4, corresponding exactly to tab, hour, and weekday from data.py. Compute logits as bias + row-wise user-video embedding dot product + the sum of the three context weights indexed by features[:, 2:]. Do not add any other feature terms.

Keep sigmoid, BCE loss, learning_rate, l2, Adam beta values, epsilon, step counting, predict output shape, and the existing Model(dimension, learning_rate=..., l2=...) constructor compatibility. Initialize embeddings with small deterministic nonzero values so the dot-product factors can learn from the first update; context weights and bias may remain zero.

Implement gradients for both embedding tables and the three context additive weights using the existing mean-BCE gradient convention, np.add.at for repeated indices, L2 regularization on trainable weights, and the same Adam update formula. Preserve finite one-dimensional logits returned by predict.
Update state() and load_state() so early stopping checkpoints and restores bias, user embeddings, video embeddings, and context weights without changing train.py.
preserve: Do not modify data.py, train.py, or config.json.
Use the existing encoded feature matrix unchanged: five columns in canonical order user_id, video_id, tab, hour, weekday, with the offsets produced by data.encode.

Retain all training and validation rows, the configured split selection, early-stopping behavior, BCE objective, optimizer settings, and prediction semantics. The model must continue to return raw logits rather than probabilities.
Do not use forbidden, excluded, or quarantined schema fields, and do not introduce source-column aliases or new data-derived features.
coordination_notes: The fixed trainer will continue calling Model(dimension, learning_rate=config["learning_rate"], l2=config["l2"]), model.step(train_features, train_labels), model.predict(valid_features), state(), and load_state(state); keep these interfaces exact.
The existing trainer will write predictions_valid.npz with row_ids=np.arange(len(valid_labels)) and scores=model.predict(valid_features); do not alter output handling or row ordering.
No configuration edit is required because embedding dimension is fixed by the experiment at 16 and must be a model implementation constant, not a new default in config.json.

reasoning: Only model_designer is activated because the exact ablation changes architecture exclusively in model.py. data.py already supplies canonical encoded user_id, video_id, tab, hour, and weekday fields, while train.py already preserves validation row order and emits the required row_ids and scores arrays. No schema-derived feature additions or configuration changes are needed.
